extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants (Korean Intellectual Property Office / Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining unity of invention among claims and rules for deposit/disclosure of microorganisms in patent applications filed in Korea; intended to direct examination practice and applicant obligations. Covers special cases (product/method/equipment/Markush/intermediate products) and procedural rules for microorganism deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity: common special technical feature among claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim (e.g. Claim 1) recites a special technical feature that is common among other claims (e.g. Claims 2 and 3), unity of inventions is met among all claims that share that common special technical feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1 = Filament A; Claim 2 = Lamp B comprising Filament A; Claim 3 = Searchlight comprising Lamp B comprising Filament A and Spinning rim C. Filament A is the common special technical feature among all claims; unity is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity: corresponding special technical features (sub-combination/combinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If different claims disclose corresponding special technical features (sub-combinations) that are technically related (e.g. timebase expander in a transmitter and timebase compressor in a receiver), unity of inventions can be met between those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1 = transmitter with timebase expander; Claim 2 = receiver with timebase compressor; Claim 3 = transmitting apparatus combining transmitter and receiver. If expander and compressor are corresponding special technical features, unity is met among Claims 1 and 2 and also among Claim 3 with Claims 1 and 2 (combination and sub-combination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity when claims recite non-identical/non-corresponding special technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claimed special technical features are not identical or do not correspond, unity is not met between claims that recite different special technical features (even if they share a common context of use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claims for control circuit A and control circuit B are different special technical features; unity is met between a control-circuit claim and an apparatus claim using that specific circuit (e.g. Claim1 and Claim3), but not between Claim1 and Claim2 (different circuits) or between apparatus claims that use different circuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity when some claims recite multiple features (combinations) vs single features
rubrics_metrics.description: When some claims recite individual features (Feature A or Feature B) and another claim recites their combination (A and B), unity is met between each single-feature claim and the combination claim, but not between the two single-feature claims themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim1 = conveyor belt with Feature A; Claim2 = conveyor belt with Feature B; Claim3 = conveyor belt with Features A and B. Unity is met between Claim1 & Claim3 and between Claim2 & Claim3, but not between Claim1 & Claim2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product vs manufacturing method: 'suitable' test for unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity between a product claim and a manufacturing-method claim of the product is determined based on whether the manufacturing method is 'suitable' for manufacturing the claimed product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Suitable' means that when the manufacturing method is practiced the product is manufactured. 'Suitable' does not require exclusivity (the product may be manufacturable by other methods and the method may be usable for other products). Examples show that a method expressly described as a method of manufacturing Product X is suitable and thus shares a common special technical feature (the product).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing-method exclusion: indirect/secondary methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacturing method must be a method of manufacturing the concerned product in itself; methods that are used indirectly or secondarily for manufacturing the product (e.g., analytical or measurement methods) shall not be filed as one application unless special conditions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should exclude indirect/secondary methods from unity grouping unless exceptional circumstances justify inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product vs method of using the product: correspondence to product qualities/functions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention of a method of using a product corresponds to using the quality or functions of the product; such method-of-use claims can correspond to product claims when the method explicitly uses the product's special qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim1 = Material A; Claim2 = method of deinsectization with Material A — Claim2 corresponds to use of Material A's insecticidal property and thus unity can be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product vs method of treating the product: definition of 'treating'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Treating the product' means applying external effects to maintain or exert the product's functions without changing its nature; methods of transfer or storage are examples and correspond to the product claim for unity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim1 = prefabricated home with special structure; Claim2 = method of storing such prefabricated home — Claim2 corresponds to treating the subject matter of Claim1 and unity is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product vs equipment for manufacturing: suitability of equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity between a product and equipment for manufacturing the product depends on whether the equipment is 'suitable' for manufacturing the product; suitability is crucial and means that when the equipment is used, the product is actually manufactured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if equipment can manufacture other products, it can still be suitable for the product of the product claim and thus unity of inventions is met. Devices only indirectly used in manufacturing (e.g., analytical devices) are not allowable as part of the same application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘Other products’ include chemical materials and microorganisms
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering equipment and other products related to manufacturing, 'other products' explicitly include chemical materials and microorganisms which can serve as manufacturing inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim1 = Antibiotic A; Claim2 = new culture B manufacturing Antibiotic A — Culture B corresponds to 'other products' manufacturing antibiotics and unity is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method vs machinery/equipment directly used to practice the method
rubrics_metrics.description: When machinery, equipment or other products are directly used for practicing a claimed method (i.e., directly used for manifestation of the method's special technical features), unity is met between the method claim and the equipment claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Suitable' for being directly used is determined by whether the equipment is directly used for manifestation of the special technical features of the method. Microorganisms used in production may be treated as manufacturing devices if their role is direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-type claims: alternatives with corresponding qualities/functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where alternative elements are recited in Markush style within a single claim, if the alternative elements have corresponding qualities or functions, unity of inventions is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Markush group includes alternative chemicals that meet the stated criteria (see other chapters), consider the group to have corresponding qualities/functions. If at least one alternative is found to lack novelty, the examiner should review unity of inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate vs end product: two-part test for unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity between intermediate materials and end products is deemed met if both (①) major structural elements between intermediate materials and end products are identical (basic chemical structure same or technically closely related providing major structural element) and (②) intermediate materials and end products are technically closely related (end products directly produced from intermediate materials or via a few identical intermediates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: amorphous polymer (intermediate) and crystalline polymer (end product) formed by orientation share major structural elements and are technically closely related so unity is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on grouping multiple intermediates/end products
rubrics_metrics.description: One application can claim more than one different intermediate material used in different processes to produce a single end material if major structural elements are identical, but more than two different intermediate materials used in other structures of end products cannot be filed as one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intermediate and end products are separated by an intermediate material that is not novel, they cannot be filed as one application. For groups of compounds, each intermediate compound should correspond to one compound in the end-product group; correspondence is required but not always possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination order: determine unity on independent claims first
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention shall be first determined on independent claims; if independent claims meet the unity requirement, dependent claims referring to them are deemed to satisfy unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If independent claim is later deleted or amended into different content, unity may no longer be satisfied and re-evaluation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity as a ground for rejection and examiner's division suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement of unity under Article 45 may constitute a ground for rejection under Article 62, and an examiner may suggest division of an application to allow the applicant a better response and facilitate speedy and accurate examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity cannot be used as a ground for provision of information or invalidation (Article 133①). Examiner may, where appropriate, notify division suggestion with the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: When dependent claims must be re-evaluated for unity due to prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: If a cited (independent) claim lacks novelty or inventive step over prior art and thus lacks 'special technical features', unity among claims depending on that cited claim cannot be assumed and dependent claims need additional review to determine whether identical or corresponding special technical features exist among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example grouping shows dependent claims split into separate invention groups when independent claim offers no improvement over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner option: notify rejection on novelty/inventive step instead of lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: If examination of dependent claims would not require additional effort despite lack of unity, the examiner may directly notify rejection based on lack of novelty/inventive step for the set of claims rather than issuing a separate lack-of-unity notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be used to streamline examination when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to deposit micro-organisms prior to filing (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person wishing to file a patent application for an invention related to a micro-organism shall deposit the micro-organism with a designated domestic depository or an international depository authority prior to filing, unless a person of ordinary skill can easily obtain the microorganism without deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit authorities are those publicly notified by the Commissioner of KIPO; exceptions apply when a microorganism is easily obtainable by skilled persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of deposit and evidential document in application
rubrics_metrics.description: When a micro-organism is deposited, the applicant shall state the deposit fact and deposit number in the patent application (in the specification) and attach document evidencing the deposit (e.g., copy of deposit receipt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the micro-organism is not deposited, the applicant must disclose how the micro-organism was acquired so a skilled person can obtain it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting change/new deposit number after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new deposit number is given for a deposited micro-organism after a patent application is filed, the applicant/patentee shall report the new deposit number to the Commissioner of KIPO without delay and attach evidential documents (Annexed form No.18, copy of new deposit certificate, and representation proof if filed by representative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to report may affect proceedings; specific forms and documents are prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 3 disclosure requirement (specification content)
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions related to micro-organisms, the applicant shall disclose the deposit number given by a domestic or international depository in the specification, or if not deposited, the method by which the applicant acquired the micro-organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure supports the requirement that the invention be described so a person skilled in the art may practice it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of deposit: supplementing description/practicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositing micro-organisms supplements the specification disclosure so that a person of ordinary skill can practice the invention when biological starting materials or end products cannot be easily practiced based solely on the written disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should deposit biological materials when detailed methods or means to obtain starting materials/end products are otherwise insufficient for practice by skilled persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligible for deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-organisms subject to deposit include biological materials such as genes, vectors, germs, mold, animal cells, fertilized eggs, seeds, etc.; eligibility varies by depository and plant-related inventions may deposit parent plants, seeds or cells as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult depository scope; deposit of appropriate starting materials enables enablement for plant-related inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositories designated and international depositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositories include domestic institutions designated by the Commissioner of KIPO (e.g., KCTC, KCCM, KACC) and international depositories recognized under the Budapest Treaty; international depositories in Korea include specified institutions (e.g., KCTC, KCCM, KCLRF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must deposit with authorities publicly notified by KIPO or recognized international depositories when deposit is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganisms 'easily secured' exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-organisms are 'easily secured' (so deposit not required) if they: (①) are currently on sale in the market; (②) are deposited at credible depositories before filing and listed in depository catalogs (with depository and deposit number disclosed in initial specification); or (③) can be easily produced by a person skilled in the art based on the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If falling under these categories, deposit may be unnecessary but the application must disclose the necessary information (catalog reference or production method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedure: evidential documents and statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants intending to file inventions related to micro-organisms shall deposit the micro-organism and attach evidential deposit document to the patent application; if the microorganism is easily obtainable by a skilled person, deposit may be omitted but the application must state how to obtain it and include deposit number in original specification if deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For divisional, converted, or priority-claim applications, the intention to rely on a deposit must be stated and proving documents attached or referenced to previously submitted documents to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit timing and priority considerations for national/international filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For national-phase entries of international applications, microorganism should be deposited to the international depositary authority before the filing date of the patent application and the intention and proving documents enclosed; for domestic priority claims, deposits in prior applications can be relied upon if deposit number disclosed in prior specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits made before the priority date and disclosed properly can convey priority effect; timely deposit is required for priority benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination rule (pre-2015): deposit certificate attachment and new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before Dec 31, 2014: if application states a deposit and deposit number but lacks copy of deposit certificate, examiner shall consider the micro-organism not deposited and proceed with examination; if applicant later attaches certificate after notification, examiner shall accept and continue. Disclosure of deposit number in an amendment to the original specification is deemed an addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name changes in depository records are acceptable if substantiated by evidential documents; however, newly disclosed scientific characteristics not in original specification constitute new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit must be completed by filing time and time-of-deposit definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit of micro-organisms is meant to supplement description so deposit must be completed by the time of filing the application; time of deposit is the date when the applicant deposits the micro-organisms and the depository receives them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only deposit number is disclosed but deposit certificate is never submitted through amendment, it shall be deemed the deposit was never made as of the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination (post-Jan-1-2015): checking deposit and proving documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed after Jan 1, 2015: formalities examination should verify microorganisms stated in proving documents are deposited before filing; deficiencies (no deposit before filing or incorrect depository name/deposit number/deposit date) should be communicated and proposed to remedy; if not remedied within time limit, proceeding related to deposit may be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to attach proving documents or indicating intention correctly can contravene rules and lead to invalidation under Article 46 formalities procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination (post-Jan-1-2015): proceed when documents are complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no deficiencies are identified in submitted deposit documents for a patent application requiring microorganism deposit, substantive examination shall be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner conducts substantive examination only after formalities defects regarding deposits are cleared.
